method.description: Coming Soon membership is a 90-day Pacific-local window over four independent evidence facts: AMC Coming Soon catalog membership, Seattle-area AMC theater bookings, TMDB US theatrical releases, and published Reel Seattle showtimes. A film with any local screening on or before the current-availability cutoff is excluded. Otherwise a local future screening yields confirmed_local and AMC catalog membership with an in-window catalog release date yields amc_announced. Those rows are user-visible unless a high-confidence presentation filter marks them as rental, untitled-placeholder, or operational SKUs. TMDB-only evidence is retained in the analysis artifact and is never user-visible.

presentation.overview: South Central LA, the early 1980s. Pierce Mundy (Everett Silas) is always on the move without ever really getting anywhere -- kept busy by his parents, their dry cleaning shop, friends and neighbors. His childhood buddies are all in prison or dead and his best friend Soldier (Ronnie Bell) is just getting out of jail. Pierce's brother Wendell (Monte Easter), on the other hand, is an up-and-coming lawyer set to marry an upper-middle-class woman (Gaye Shannon-Burnett). Pierce is entirely lacking in ambition, to the consternation of his Bible-thumping mother (Jessie Holmes), and yet he is an integral part of life in the neighborhood. When Soldier is killed in a car accident, Pierce's conflicting obligations to family and friends manifest in the choice between his brother's wedding and his best friend's funeral, both falling on the same day. Charles Burnett's second feature after Killer of Sheep is a tragicomic classic of New Black Cinema in which lived realities are shown in even the smallest of supporting roles, complex and attentive. Pierce's wanderings reveal a portrait of a young man and a community defined in equal measure by stagnation, resignation, resistance and joie de vivre.

Told through the eyes of wildlife species ranging from the mysterious blind catfish to the elusive mountain lion, the story follows our ever-changing relationship with the natural world and showcases our ability to destroy, conserve, and recover wildlife and the habitat we mutually depend on.

Narrated by Matthew McConaughey and featuring state-of-the-art cinematography, this family-friendly film journeys from the highest peaks in West Texas, through our aquifers, rivers, and bays, and deep into the Gulf of Mexico. Deep in the Heart aims to conserve our remaining wild places, to show the connectivity of water and wildlife, and to recognize Texas -  conservation importance on a continental scale.

presentation.overview:
Begotten has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures:

God Killing Himself. 
Mother Earth. 
Son of Earth -- Flesh on Bone. 

The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. 

God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth -- Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed, and briefly returned to life by his mother. The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down, and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.


Begotten was shot in black and white on 16mm reversal film, then rephotographed frame by frame through neutral-density filters. The process took four years and roughly ten hours of work for every finished minute. 

The image was worked by hand through repeated exposure through neutral density filtrations until the grain itself began to move like an atmospheric condition, thickening the dark and tearing open the light.

As they navigate the war-torn streets of Baghdad, the family is trapped in a firefight between U.S. Marines and insurgents, and one Marine's split-second decision devastates the family. Years later, haunted by his time in Iraq and aided by a New Yorker journalist, the Marine seeks to reconcile with the Khachaturian matriarch and her surviving family members. Anchored by moving, unforgettable performances from Boyd Holbrook, Hiam Abbass, and Kenneth Branagh, Atonement is a powerfully human story about the immeasurable costs of war, exploring universal questions about guilt, redemption, and the nature of forgiveness.

entries.title: Islande a velo - au gre du vent - Les aventuriers voyageurs

presentation.overview:
"Au Gre du Vent" tells the somewhat crazy story of an unlikely cycling duo: two men who could have been father and son, united by a taste for adventure and a desire to push their limits. Together, they embark on a challenge they had somewhat underestimated: cycling around Iceland. As the kilometers unfold, they discover an island as magnificent as it is untamed. Between volcanoes, glaciers, lava fields, and ocean-battered cliffs, the landscapes offer a breathtaking spectacle. But Iceland's wild beauty comes at a price: violent winds, persistent rain, and unpredictable weather transform each stage into a true challenge!

Fueled by humor, friendship, and determination, the two cyclists journey with the wind, experiencing moments of wonder and unexpected challenges. A human and visual adventure that reminds us that the most beautiful journeys are often those we hadn't quite planned.

presentation.overview: On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the Nepstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans. The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favorite tracks--'Bohemian Rhapsody,' 'Crazy Little Thing Called Love,' 'I Want To Break Free' and 'We Are The Champions.' With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the country's top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity

ALWAYS LALISA is a feature-length documentary following global superstar LISA during a transformative year away from Blackpink, the K-pop phenomenon that made her one of the world's most recognizable performers. As the group pauses activities, LISA embarks on the first true chapter of her solo career, confronting the question of who she is beyond Blackpink.

The film follows LISA as she writes, records, and releases her debut solo album, Alter Ego, makes her acting debut in the third season of The White Lotus, and prepares for her first major solo performance at the 2025 Coachella Music Festival. Born and raised in Thailand, LISA left home at fourteen to train in South Korea's demanding K-pop system, ultimately rising to global superstardom. But forging her own path, particularly in the Western music market, brings new pressures, relentless scrutiny, and the challenge of redefining herself on her own terms.

Intimate, emotional, and revealing, Always Lalisa captures an artist at a crossroads, documenting a year of risk, reinvention, and self-discovery as LISA begins to define not only her next chapter, but the woman and artist she wants to become.

As the group pauses activities, LISA embarks on the first true chapter of her solo career, confronting the question of who she is beyond Blackpink.

The film follows LISA as she writes, records, and releases her debut solo album, Alter Ego, makes her acting debut in the third season of The White Lotus, and prepares for her first major solo performance at the 2025 Coachella Music Festival. Born and raised in Thailand, LISA left home at fourteen to train in South Korea's demanding K-pop system, ultimately rising to global superstardom. But forging her own path, particularly in the Western music market, brings new pressures, relentless scrutiny, and the challenge of redefining herself on her own terms.

Intimate, emotional, and revealing, Always Lalisa captures an artist at a crossroads, documenting a year of risk, reinvention, and self-discovery as LISA begins to define not only her next chapter, but the woman and artist she wants to become.

The film that launched the Kendrick Brothers into becoming some of the leading faith-based filmmakers in the world for the last two decades, Flywheel, has been reimagined by Brazilian filmmakers under the Kendricks' direct guidance. The project emerged out of the Kendrick Brothers' growing impact in Brazil. Their 2024 film, The Forge, opened in the Brazilian market at #1 and greatly exceeded box-office expectations. While promoting The Forge release, Alex and Stephen Kendrick connected with leaders across the country who expressed a growing need for locally rooted, faith-driven content.  From those conversations, a Brazilian FLYWHEEL remake was born. 

Set in Rio de Janeiro, the new film FLYWHEEL: IGNITION OF THE SOUL follows Noah Silva, a smooth-talking, used-car salesman whose "do whatever it takes" approach to business and life begins to unravel at home and at work.  After a series of wake-up calls, Noah is forced to confront the cost of his choices. He begins a difficult and deeply personal journey to restore his integrity while trying to win back the hearts of his wife and son.

Sparkling, dizzying, and deliciously potent, FALLEN ANGELS, Noel Coward's champagne-fresh comedy of bad manners, shocked and delighted audiences at its 1925 premiere. Two upper-class wives, their husbands away for the day, share a few toasts to their pre-marital dalliances--with the same man, who just may be en route from France to visit. Old rivalries and past scandals bubble to the surface in this intoxicating romp from one of theatre's comedy masters.

Starring Golden Globe-winner Rose Byrne (If I Had Legs I'd Kick You) and Tony Award winner Kelli O'Hara (The King and I), with Tracee Chimo, Mark Consuelos (making his Broadway debut), Christopher Fitzgerald and Aasif Mandvi, this new Roundabout Theatre and Tony Award-winning production of 'pure escapist fun' (The New York Times) was filmed live on stage at Broadway's Todd Haimes Theatre and now comes to the big screen.

FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Huller) - actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins - from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US,
Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

With FATHERLAND, Pawlikowski picks up where he left off with his award-winning Ida and ColdWar, exploring -- in his elliptic, distilled style - the themes of identity, family, love and guilt amid the turmoil and confusion of post-war Europe.

presentation.overview:
In 2005, Sofia Coppola shot her third feature film, Marie Antoinette, starring Kirsten Dunst and Jason Schwartzman, at the Palace of Versailles, securing unprecedented filming permission that had never before been granted to any production. Her mother, acclaimed documentarian Eleanor Coppola, accompanied her on set, capturing approximately eighty hours of footage chronicling her daughter's journey throughout the making of the film. This year, on the occasion of the 20th anniversary of the release of Marie Antoinette and in fulfilment of her mother's wish, Sofia Coppola edited that previously unseen material. Making Marie Antoinette explores the craftsmanship and care that brought the film to life, follows legendary costume designer Milena Canonero at work, and offers a glimpse into what it meant to be a young female director at that time. The result is a fascinating look at the creative process behind a landmark film and, at the same time, a surprisingly intimate family portrait.

In the documentary, Eleanor Coppola's voice is performed by Academy Award nominee Diane Lane, who reads excerpts from Eleanor's diaries, in which the filmmaker recounts her experience on set and reflects on her relationship with her daughter.

presentation.overview:
If you're nice, you get presents from the Big Guy. If you're naughty, you get justice.

David Harbour reprises his role as Santa Claus in a propulsive new chapter in yuletide mayhem from 87North--the powerhouse producers of Bullet Train, John Wick, The Fall Guy, Atomic Blonde and the Nobody franchise--and returning action director Tommy Wirkola.

In 2022's bare-knuckle holiday sensation, VIOLENT NIGHT, an embittered Santa, armed with lethal combat skills, took out a team of mercenaries to rescue a girl and her family. Now, not-so-jolly Saint Nick suits up again to take on a ruthless gangster (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Jared Harris) terrorizing the merchants of the Silver Bell Mall.

But when Santa forgets the true meaning of Christmas, he finds himself in the heart of a lively mall community in desperate need of his help. Sapped of his magic, he'll need another way to take on the goons threatening the mall, and time is running out. Santa has to rediscover his faith in goodness and call in some last-minute reinforcements from the one person no baddie wants to tangle with: Mrs. Claus (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Kristen Bell). 

Along with David Harbour, Jared Harris and Kristen Bell, the dynamic cast includes Emmy winning screen legend Joe Pantoliano (The Last of Us, The Sopranos), Daniela Melchior (Fast X, Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3), Andrew Bachelor (Greenland, The Walking Dead), and AEW professional wrestler Maxwell Friedman (The Iron Claw, Happy Gilmore 2).

VIOLENT NIGHT 2 is directed by returning filmmaker Tommy Wirkola and produced again by 87North founders Kelly McCormick and David Leitch. The film's returning screenwriters are Pat Casey and Josh Miller. Violent Night 2 will be released by Universal Pictures.
